construct: Fractional-cent residue accumulator in an OS Sort E35 output exit that is reset on a sort work-dataset boundary instead of only at end-of-merge
description: CABSE35B is the E35 output exit named by MODS=(E35=(CABSE35B,4096)) on the sort control card JCL/CTLCARDS/CABSRT07. It is entered once per record leaving the final merge, after SUM FIELDS has already collapsed duplicate keys into one summary line per BAN and jurisdiction. P3000-APPLY-ROUNDING applies the record's own RT-ROUND-RULE to the summed five-decimal amount and stores a two-decimal result in LK-SM-ROUNDED. The fraction given up by that rounding is computed as WS-RESIDUE = WS-RAW-AMT - WS-BACK-TO-FIVE and added to WS-RESIDUE-ACC by P4000-ACCUM-RESIDUE. At end of merge (null record address in word one of the parameter list) P8000-END-OF-MERGE builds one residue adjustment record from WS-RESIDUE-ACC, points word one at it and replies return code 08 so the sort writes it to SORTOUT. That is the 1991 tariff requirement: fractional cents must be carried to the invoice total rather than discarded per line. P2000-WORK-BOUNDARY, added in 2008, reads LK-RC-WORK-ORD out of the 12-byte rating control prefix that CABSE35A stamped into bytes 189-200 of every record. That field carries the ordinal of the sort work dataset the record came out of, stepped by CABSE35A each time the string limit (65,000 records since the 2015 region change) is reached. When P2000-WORK-BOUNDARY sees the ordinal change it calls P2400-RESTART-RESIDUE, which adds the accumulated value to WS-RESIDUE-DISCARDED (a display-only field) and then MOVEs ZERO to WS-RESIDUE-ACC and to WS-RESIDUE-LINES. The comment justifies this as preventing a double count where the merge re-presents the high key of one string as the low key of the next. That justification is false - SUM FIELDS has already run and no key is presented twice - but it is plausible enough that it survived a 2008 review. The consequence is that only the residue accumulated within the final sort work dataset ever reaches the adjustment record. Everything accumulated in every earlier string is discarded. A sort that fits in one work dataset never steps the ordinal past 01, so P2400-RESTART-RESIDUE is never entered and the exit is exactly correct. The defect is therefore invisible in every low-volume test, every unit test, every parallel run on a subset, and every cycle small enough to sort in memory or in a single SORTWK. It appears only when the summary file is large enough to spill, and the amount lost grows with the number of spills.
business_impact: The rounding adjustment line on the invoice understates the accumulated fractional cents by the residue of every sort string except the last. With roughly 65,000 summary lines per work dataset and a mean residue of about half a cent per rounded line, each discarded string loses on the order of USD 150-300 of adjustment, and a large cycle spilling to six or eight work datasets loses that five to seven times over. The loss is systematically in one direction - always against the amount carried to the invoice total - because the residue is a positive accumulation of discarded fractions. It is not a rounding wobble that averages out. Three properties make it very hard to find: (1) the control framework does not see it, because a sort step writes no CABS-CONTROL-RECORD and the balancing equation CT-READ = CT-WRITTEN + CT-REJECTED + CT-SUMMARISED + CT-CARRIED-FWD is evaluated by CABRAT09 on the records the sort handed it, which are internally consistent; (2) the bill still foots, because the summary lines and the adjustment line agree with each other - it is only the relationship to the unrounded detail that is broken; (3) it scales with volume, so it appears first and worst on the largest carriers, which are exactly the accounts where a carrier's own bill verification is most likely to find it and raise a dispute. WS-RESIDUE-DISCARDED is printed to SYSOUT at end of merge under the label 'PRIOR STRNG', so the evidence has existed on every sort listing since 2008 and has never been read.
correct_modernization_response: First, recognise that the rule lives in the exit at all. CABRAT09 contains no rounding of the summary-level amount; a reviewer reading the COBOL alone will conclude the summary is unrounded and will reimplement it that way, losing both the rounding and the residue. The rounding rule, the residue accumulation and the adjustment record must be extracted from CABSE35B and restated as explicit, testable pipeline stages before anything is rewritten. Second, the residue accumulator must be scoped to the business boundary it belongs to - the invoice, or the run - and never to a physical artefact of the sort. In target state the accumulation should be an explicit aggregate over the summary rows for an account and period, computed after the aggregation and before the invoice total is struck, with no dependence on partitioning, spill behaviour, parallelism or arrival order. Third, the whole coupling through the 12-byte rating control prefix should be removed: CABSE35A stamps it, no copybook describes it, no COBOL program reads it, and CABSE35B silently depends on it across two different sort steps. Fourth, the correct fix in place - if the estate is to be kept running while it is migrated - is to delete P2400-RESTART-RESIDUE entirely and reset WS-RESIDUE-ACC only in P1000-INIT; the double-count the comment describes does not occur. Finally, a regression test must be built at a volume that forces the sort to spill (more than one SORTWK), because no test below that volume can distinguish the defective and correct versions.
